children: Copper prices fell on Tuesday to their lowest levels in more than three weeks as inventories at the London Metal Exchange rose, growth concerns from higher oil prices escalated and the dollar climbed.

on the London Metal Exchange firmed 0.1% to $14,021 a metric ton at 1006 GMT as bargain hunters entered the fray, traders said. Earlier in the session it dropped to $13,926, the lowest since August 20.
Copper stocks in LME registered warehouses have risen nearly 20% tons since the middle of August to 242,900 tons, due to elevated premiums for nearby contracts against longer-dated forwards

Traders expect more copper sold at previously high prices to be delivered to LME warehouses over coming days. But with the premiums flipping into discounts last week deliveries are likely to dry up pretty quickly, they added.
Copper prices across maturities started to fall last week after sources told Reuters U.S. President Donald Trump had not yet made a decision on whether to impose tariffs on copper imports.

The possibility of tariffs on U.S. copper imports pushed Comex copper prices to levels above LME prices. Traders have, for the past 18 months, shipped copper to the United States, taking Comex stocks to record highs (HG-STX-COMEX).

"Nothing good can come of confusing markets with what is essentially government policy," said Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price. "My gut feeling is he will impose it at some point otherwise we're going to see the biggest trade reversal in the history of copper."
Analysts say concerns about oil supplies and prices at around $107 a barrel
, up from near $87 a barrel at the end of August, will weigh on growth, manufacturing activity and demand for metals.
Overall industrial metals came under pressure from the firmer U.S. currency, which makes dollar-priced commodities more expensive for holder of other currencies.
